title: Board Composition: Appointment, Tenure, Succession and Diversity
summary: How to build a board with the right mix of skills, independence and perspectives, the due diligence a director should complete before accepting an appointment, and how to manage tenure, refreshment and succession.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to build a board with the right mix of skills, independence and perspectives, the due diligence a director should complete before accepting an appointment, and how to manage tenure, refreshment and succession.
Learning Objectives: Design a board composition and skills matrix for a regulated firm or fund
Carry out due diligence before accepting a board appointment
Plan tenure, refreshment, succession and diversity objectives
Syllabus: Board size, balance of non-executive and independent directors, and skills matrices
Due diligence before accepting an offer: good practice and red flags
Tenure limits, board refreshment and succession planning
Diversity of skills, background and thinking, barriers and effective initiatives
Intended Audience: Chairs, executive, non-executive and independent directors of regulated firms, fund boards and management companies
Senior managers preparing for a first board appointment or moving from an executive to a non-executive role
Company secretaries, heads of governance and compliance staff who support the board and its committees
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No prior governance training is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Examination of Governance for Collective Investment Schemes (2006–2007)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
Olivier Sibony, You're About to Make a Terrible Mistake! How Biases Distort Decision-Making (2020)
